AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #2
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. About how high should a compost heap be built? (1 mark)
   A. About as high as your chest
   B. As flat as the ground
   C. As high as a house
   D. Only one hand high

2. What is soil erosion? (1 mark)
   A. Planting trees
   B. Watering the garden
   C. Adding manure to soil
   D. The washing or blowing away of top soil

3. What is the meaning of conserving water? (1 mark)
   A. Storing dirty water
   B. Using it carefully so none is wasted
   C. Using as much as possible
   D. Selling water

4. How far from the plant should the bottle drip be placed? (1 mark)
   A. Exactly on top of the stem
   B. In the next field
   C. About 10 to 15 cm
   D. Two metres

5. Which of these is a way of collecting water for the garden? (1 mark)
   A. Digging up rivers
   B. Burning the roof
   C. Collecting rainwater from a roof
   D. Cutting down trees

6. What is drip irrigation? (1 mark)
   A. Spraying water high into the air
   B. Flooding the whole field
   C. Letting water fall slowly drop by drop near the roots
   D. Throwing water from a bucket quickly

7. Why is dry firewood better than wet firewood? (1 mark)
   A. It is heavier
   B. It cannot burn
   C. It burns better with less smoke
   D. It puts out fires

8. Which tool should an adult use to help fix the scarecrow pole? (1 mark)
   A. A knife on the pole
   B. A tin of paint
   C. A bare hand only
   D. A hammer or heavy stone to push it in

9. What word means living peacefully together with wild animals? (1 mark)
   A. Poaching
   B. Hunting
   C. Trapping
   D. Coexisting

10. What is a wild animal? (1 mark)
   A. An animal kept for milk
   B. An animal kept in a house
   C. An animal sold in shops
   D. An animal that lives freely in nature

11. Which of these is a peaceful way of protecting fruit from birds? (1 mark)
   A. Covering trees with a light net
   B. Burning the trees
   C. Poisoning the birds
   D. Setting traps that kill

12. Why should tiny seeds not be sown deeply? (1 mark)
   A. They run out of stored food before reaching the light
   B. They become large
   C. They wash away
   D. They grow faster

13. Why are carrots not transplanted? (1 mark)
   A. Moving damages the root and makes it crooked
   B. They grow in water
   C. They are too large
   D. They have no roots

14. Why should fruit be washed before eating? (1 mark)
   A. To make it sour
   B. To make it dry
   C. To remove dirt and germs
   D. To change its colour

15. What is the main job of the trunk of a tree? (1 mark)
   A. Collect rain
   B. Carry water and food between roots and leaves
   C. Make flowers
   D. Absorb sunlight

16. What is topsoil? (1 mark)
   A. A fertiliser
   B. The bottom layer
   C. Sand from the river
   D. The dark top layer of soil

17. What do roots of a fruit tree do? (1 mark)
   A. Collect sunlight
   B. Produce seeds
   C. Make fruits
   D. Hold the tree and take in water and food

18. Why should young fruit trees be watered in dry weather? (1 mark)
   A. Their roots are small and cannot reach much water
   B. Water kills them
   C. They do not need water
   D. Water makes fruit sour

19. Which is an example of caring for fruit plants? (1 mark)
   A. Watering, weeding and mulching
   B. Burning the leaves
   C. Cutting the roots
   D. Leaving them without water

20. Which domestic animal is kept as a pet to guard the home? (1 mark)
   A. Goat
   B. Dog
   C. Cow
   D. Hen

21. What is the young one of a hen called? (1 mark)
   A. Lamb
   B. Kid
   C. Calf
   D. Chick

22. Who should be called when a cow is sick? (1 mark)
   A. A driver
   B. A carpenter
   C. A veterinary officer
   D. A tailor

23. What is the young one of a cow called? (1 mark)
   A. Calf
   B. Kid
   C. Lamb
   D. Chick

24. Which drink is best with meals? (1 mark)
   A. Only soda
   B. Clean water
   C. Dirty water
   D. Only sugary juice

25. Which of these can happen if a child eats only ugali? (1 mark)
   A. Feeling weak and getting sick often
   B. Never feeling tired
   C. Getting all vitamins
   D. Growing very tall at once

26. What do protective foods do? (1 mark)
   A. Give all the body's energy
   B. Help the body to fight sickness
   C. Build walls
   D. Store water

27. Which activity is part of keeping a food journal? (1 mark)
   A. Writing what you eat at each meal
   B. Buying food
   C. Throwing food away
   D. Cooking only

28. Which food may be served with boiled potatoes for a balanced meal? (1 mark)
   A. Sugar
   B. Vegetable stew
   C. Soda only
   D. A second helping of potatoes only

29. Why do we cook food? (1 mark)
   A. To make it soft, tasty and safe to eat
   B. To make it dirty
   C. To make it colder
   D. To make it disappear

30. What should you do before you start cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Play with the fire
   B. Wash your hands
   C. Eat first
   D. Take off your shoes

31. How can you tell that water is boiling? (1 mark)
   A. The water is still
   B. The water is cold
   C. Big bubbles rise quickly and steam comes off
   D. The water is blue

32. Which is a disadvantage of too much frying? (1 mark)
   A. It removes all flavour
   B. Too much oil is not good for health
   C. It makes food cold
   D. It uses no heat

33. Why should you not dip hands into a drinking water container? (1 mark)
   A. The container would break
   B. Hands may put germs into the water
   C. Hands would get cold
   D. The water would evaporate

34. Why should you bathe every day? (1 mark)
   A. To waste water
   B. To remove sweat, dirt and germs
   C. To make the body hot
   D. To make skin dry

35. Why should the compound be free of long grass and rubbish? (1 mark)
   A. Snakes, rats and mosquitoes can hide there
   B. It looks colourful
   C. To save soap
   D. To stop rain

36. How should gumboots be dried? (1 mark)
   A. In a closed cupboard while wet
   B. Under a heavy weight
   C. Beside a hot fire
   D. Upside down in a shady, airy place

37. What is personal protective equipment? (1 mark)
   A. Soap for cleaning
   B. Food for health
   C. Tools for digging
   D. Clothing and gear worn to protect the body

38. Which is a mistake in tacking? (1 mark)
   A. Marking the line first
   B. Using small back stitch at the end
   C. Making stitches of different lengths in even tacking
   D. Using contrasting thread

39. How much of each edge is folded twice for the handkerchief hem? (1 mark)
   A. 10 cm
   B. About 1 cm each time
   C. 1 mm
   D. 20 cm

40. What size square did we cut for the handkerchief? (1 mark)
   A. 5 m by 5 m
   B. 1 m by 1 m
   C. 2 cm by 2 cm
   D. 25 cm by 25 cm

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Give three mistakes to avoid when sowing tiny seeds. (3 marks)

42. Describe how to make long and short tacking. (4 marks)

43. Why should kerosene never be poured onto a fire? (2 marks)

44. Describe how to wash hands correctly. (4 marks)

45. Plan a weekly cleaning schedule for the classroom using dusting, sweeping, mopping and refuse disposal. (5 marks)

46. Explain why it is best to choose fruits that suit your locality. (3 marks)

47. Explain what a fruit is in plant growth. (2 marks)

48. Name three foods that are boiled. (3 marks)

49. State two safety rules when making a scarecrow. (2 marks)

50. Give two disadvantages of shallow frying. (2 marks)

51. Name three products we get from cattle. (3 marks)

52. Explain how animals help crops grow. (3 marks)

53. Choose PPE for gardening and say why. (3 marks)

54. Give three uses of tacking stitches. (3 marks)

55. Give three benefits of using compost manure on the farm. (3 marks)

56. Give three good personal hygiene practices apart from washing hands. (3 marks)

57. A family boils beans for a long time on a big fire with the lid off. Suggest five ways to improve fuel use. (5 marks)

58. List three things needed to make a bucket drip system. (3 marks)

59. Why do we need protective foods? (2 marks)

60. Name two problems that can attack ripe fruits. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #2 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — About as high as your chest
   A heap that is too low loses heat and one that is too high is hard to turn.

2. D — The washing or blowing away of top soil
   Bare soil can be carried away by rain or wind.

3. B — Using it carefully so none is wasted
   Conserving means saving and protecting.

4. C — About 10 to 15 cm
   Close enough for the roots to reach the water.

5. C — Collecting rainwater from a roof
   Rainwater tanks store water for dry days.

6. C — Letting water fall slowly drop by drop near the roots
   Drip irrigation gives small amounts of water directly at the roots.

7. C — It burns better with less smoke
   Dry wood gives more heat and less smoke.

8. D — A hammer or heavy stone to push it in
   An adult helps with heavy or sharp work.

9. D — Coexisting
   To coexist is to live together.

10. D — An animal that lives freely in nature
   Wild animals are not kept by people.

11. A — Covering trees with a light net
   A net keeps birds away without harming them.

12. A — They run out of stored food before reaching the light
   Deep seeds cannot push up to the surface.

13. A — Moving damages the root and makes it crooked
   The carrot root is the food, so it must grow straight.

14. C — To remove dirt and germs
   Clean fruit is safe to eat.

15. B — Carry water and food between roots and leaves
   The trunk is like a pipe for the plant.

16. D — The dark top layer of soil
   Topsoil is rich in plant food.

17. D — Hold the tree and take in water and food
   Roots anchor and absorb.

18. A — Their roots are small and cannot reach much water
   Young trees are easily stressed by drought.

19. A — Watering, weeding and mulching
   Care keeps plants healthy.

20. B — Dog
   Dogs guard homes.

21. D — Chick
   A chick is a young chicken.

22. C — A veterinary officer
   A vet treats sick animals.

23. A — Calf
   A calf is a young cow or bull.

24. B — Clean water
   Water is essential and healthy.

25. A — Feeling weak and getting sick often
   One food cannot supply all nutrients.

26. B — Help the body to fight sickness
   Vitamins and minerals help protect health.

27. A — Writing what you eat at each meal
   Records help you check your meals.

28. B — Vegetable stew
   Vegetables add protective foods.

29. A — To make it soft, tasty and safe to eat
   Heat kills germs and softens food.

30. B — Wash your hands
   Clean hands prevent germs.

31. C — Big bubbles rise quickly and steam comes off
   These are signs of boiling.

32. B — Too much oil is not good for health
   Too much oil can harm health.

33. B — Hands may put germs into the water
   Use a clean cup or tap.

34. B — To remove sweat, dirt and germs
   Bathing keeps the body clean.

35. A — Snakes, rats and mosquitoes can hide there
   A tidy compound is safer.

36. D — Upside down in a shady, airy place
   This drains water and protects the rubber.

37. D — Clothing and gear worn to protect the body
   PPE protects us from harm.

38. C — Making stitches of different lengths in even tacking
   Stitches should be equal.

39. B — About 1 cm each time
   The raw edge is hidden.

40. D — 25 cm by 25 cm
   A small handkerchief is easy to make.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Leaving big lumps in the seedbed, sowing too deep, sowing too thick without thinning, or watering strongly (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each mistake.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Mark a line; make a long stitch of about 2 cm on top; make a short stitch of about 0.5 cm underneath; repeat along the line; finish with a small back stitch.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: It catches fire quickly and can burst into flames and burn people.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for catching fire, 1 mark for danger.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Wet hands; use soap; rub palms, backs of hands, between fingers, thumbs and nails for about 20 seconds; rinse; dry with a clean cloth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four correct steps.

45. (5 marks)
   Answer: A table of days with jobs for each learner group: Monday dusting, Tuesday sweeping, Wednesday mopping, and refuse disposal each day, with tools and safety measures.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for jobs, 1 for tools, 1 for safety, 1 for fairness of sharing.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: They grow better in the local climate, give more fruit, and need less care and cost.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct reason.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: The part of a plant that holds the seeds.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for part of a plant, 1 mark for holding seeds.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Potatoes, eggs, cassava, maize, beans, rice (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each food.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: Ask an adult to help with sharp or heavy work; do not use wire or broken glass; wear gloves for rough poles (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

50. (2 marks)
   Answer: It can splash and burn, and too much oil is not good for health.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each disadvantage.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Milk, beef, hides and skins, manure, or draught power (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each product.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: Their dung is used as manure, which feeds the soil, and oxen can be used to plough. Crops then grow well.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for manure, 1 for ploughing, 1 for better crops.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: Gloves protect hands from dirt and cuts; gumboots protect feet from mud; hat protects the head from the sun.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each item with reason.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Hold layers of cloth together, mark a line, keep hems in place, help to sew straight (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each use.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: It feeds crops, it softens the soil and helps it to hold water, and it is cheap because it uses waste.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct benefit.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Bathing daily, brushing teeth twice a day, keeping nails short, wearing clean clothes, drinking safe water (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

57. (5 marks)
   Answer: Soak the beans first, cook with the lid on, use dry wood, reduce the flame after boiling starts, cut food or use an improved jiko, put out the fire after cooking.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: A bucket or container, a hose or pipe, and small holes or drippers for water to come out. A stand may also be used.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each item.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: They give vitamins and minerals that fight sickness and keep the body healthy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for fight sickness, 1 mark for vitamins or minerals.

60. (2 marks)
   Answer: Fruit flies, birds or monkeys (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
